issuingEntity: SHIFT DAO LLC, a for-profit series DAO limited liability company. Each product is a separate designated Series of that LLC (Series 12-18 observed) with its own executed Series Operating Agreement; the Company enters each agreement "solely in its limited and non-discretionary capacity as the administrative agent" and is "not a manager, managing member, fiduciary, or controlling person" of the Series. The initial nominee member of each Series is MINS LLC, Trust Company Complex, Ajeltake Road, Ajeltake Island, Majuro, MH 96960, which "holds its membership interest solely for purposes of facilitating the formation and annual renewal" and "has no economic entitlement or discretionary authority". The Series 17 agreement is digitally signed 2026-04-19 by Robin Van Niekerk on behalf of MINS LLC. No director, officer or operating-company entity is named; the team page lists twelve individuals with no roles and cites backgrounds at the Israel Securities Authority, Tel-Aviv Stock Exchange, Deloitte, Kraken, Flow Traders, Securitize, CheckPoint, Utila and Emurgo, and names SNZ Holding as seed-round lead investor. The entity that actually holds the backing ETFs is not named: the Solution Overview says only that "SHIFT engages with a private entity that holds the backing assets".
entityJurisdiction: Republic of the Marshall Islands. Formed under the Decentralized Autonomous Organization Act 2022 and governed under the Limited Liability Company Act 1996, with the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act also cited in the Series agreements. Series segregation is asserted under LLC Act s.79. The Principal Office "need not be in the Marshall Islands" and the "Official Online Venue" for member participation is www.Shiftrwa.xyz.
governingLaw: Laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, stated in both the Terms of Use (s.12) and each Series Operating Agreement (Art. XII.2). Recourse is narrow: after a 30-day notice period a dispute "shall be settled by arbitration administered by the International Centre for Dispute Resolution", seated in the RMI, sole arbitrator, English, final and without appeal, and "No action at law or in equity based upon any claim arising out of or related to this Agreement shall be instituted in any court of any jurisdiction". The Terms of Use separately submit website disputes to "the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of RMI". Members owe and are owed no fiduciary duty (Art. IV.3, DAO Act s.109), and under Art. VI.2 (DAO Act s.111) "no one shall have the right under the LLC Act to demand to separately inspect or copy records" of the Series. A THIRD regime exists on the same issuer's vaults-only Terms, and it differs from both of the above: arbitration is "finally settled under the Rules of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce by one or more arbitrators appointed in accordance with the said Rules", with the seat "agreed by the parties" rather than fixed in the RMI, the same RMI governing law "without regard to its conflict of law principles", and - unlike the Series agreements - an express class waiver: "You agree that any disputes will be resolved on an individual basis, and you waive any right to participate in a class action lawsuit or class-wide arbitration." So one legal entity operates three inconsistent dispute regimes: ICDR with an RMI seat and a total court bar for a Series member, ICC with a negotiable seat and a class waiver for a vaults depositor, and the exclusive jurisdiction of the RMI courts for a website user. The Series agreements contain no class or consolidation provision at all, so collective redress there is unaddressed rather than waived - though sole-arbitrator bilateral arbitration reaches the same result.
regulatoryStatus: Unregistered and self-disclaiming, on top of a real company-law registration. The site-wide legal notice states the tokens "have not been registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933 ... or under the securities or financial-instrument laws of any other jurisdiction", that the issuer "is not registered or authorized as an investment company under the U.S. Investment Company Act of 1940 ... and is not authorized as an Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), an Undertaking for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS), or an investment firm under the laws of any EEA Member State", and that the tokens are "not offered, sold, or distributed in the United States or the United Kingdom, nor to any U.S. or U.K. persons or entities; in applicable jurisdictions they are offered only to 'qualified investors,' 'professional clients,' or their equivalent legal analogues". The Terms of Use add that the membership interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law, but purchasers are responsible for assessing their legal status in their jurisdiction". No prospectus, offering document or exemption filing was located in any jurisdiction, and no licence for the Series tokens - but a licence CLAIM does exist, on a different product's page. The vaults-only Terms state: "Shift DAO LLC is a corporate entity in RMI with an international investment business license and registration number 10246-26.", with a Majuro registered address (PO Box 852, Long Island Rd) and physical address (852 Lagoon Rd). Three things qualify it. (1) SCOPE: that page governs Shift Vaults - stablecoin staking and secured lending to a Cayman SPC - not the leveraged Series tokens in this dossier, and no licence claim appears in any Series Operating Agreement, in the Terms of Use, in the Risk Disclosure or in the site-wide legal notice, all of which instead deny registered or authorised status. (2) VERIFICATION: the number could not be checked against any Marshall Islands register - no public searchable register of RMI international investment business licences was located - so it is recorded as unverified, not as false. (3) CONSISTENCY: an investment-business licence, if real, would sit oddly beside the same issuer's statement that the interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law".
holderClaim: On paper: a membership interest in a designated Series of SHIFT DAO LLC whose sole purpose is to "acquire, hold, and maintain in its treasury assets whose economic performance corresponds to" one named index or stock. The Series 17 agreement says "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and Art. IV.1 says "Series Members are granted treasury ownership only", with no voting, management or fiduciary rights. In practice three things break that chain. (1) The issuer's own site-wide legal notice says the opposite: "The Series tokens provide their holders with economic exposure to the value of the Series Assets; holding the Tokens does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets." (2) The executed Series agreements do not identify the token they govern - membership is obtained by holding a token "created from and constricted by the parameters defined in the Smart Contract located at an address and a blockchain to be determined" - so no published document links the SPL mint that trades on Jupiter to the Series whose treasury holds the asset; the Series 17 (S&P 500) agreement compounds this by requiring "at least one (1) TSLA Short SHFT Token". (3) What the Series is documented to hold is not the referenced equity but a daily-reset leveraged ETF share (Series 17: SPXL, Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3x, ISIN US25459W8626; Series 12: Direxion Daily TSLA X2, ISIN US25460G2865), so exposure to Tesla or the S&P 500 is delivered through a third party's derivative fund. Graded as derivative for that reason; if the Series agreements' "owners in the Series Assets" language controlled and were bound to these mints, the record would move to spv-claim-redeemable.
underlyingCustodian: Two custodians are named, in the Risk Disclosure only: "Each Series relies on DekaBank, a European regulated financial institution, and ALPACADB LTD, a U.S.-regulated broker, as custodians of the Series Assets." The Collateral & Custody page adds that backing is held "with FINRA-registered, SEC-regulated brokerage partners" in "dedicated accounts, separate from operational balances and from other clients' assets" and "off-balance-sheet". Marketing and press name Alpaca Markets as the brokerage rail. The holding entity itself is not named ("a private entity that holds the backing assets"), nor is the market maker that operates the B2B mint/burn endpoints, and no account, statement, holdings report or balance for any Series has been published.

custodyVerification.agent: Chainlink Proof-of-Reserves is claimed as the verification agent and no such feed exists. Re-verified directly on 2026-09-18: Chainlink's own reference-data directory carries no SHIFT feed on either network (295 Ethereum-mainnet feeds, 12 Solana-mainnet feeds; the single "shift" string match is Coinshift's USPC NAV feed), no contract and no report was located, and the integration has been forthcoming since 2025-05-21
custodyVerification.frequency: claimed continuous - "The feed publishes the verified reserve state on-chain, every block" - but nothing observed at any cadence
custodyVerification.notes: Claimed, not evidenced. The docs assert Chainlink PoR "runs continuously, verifying that every Series Token in circulation is backed 1:1" and that "the SHIFT smart contract cannot issue tokens in excess of verified reserves; mint operations are gated by PoR feed". Verified 2026-09-16 and re-verified 2026-09-17: the PoR dashboard link on that same page still reads "[TO BE UPDATED]" and the third-party attestation section still reads "[TO BE UPDATED]", and no Chainlink PoR feed naming SHIFT could be found. The app dashboard link has changed: on 2026-09-16 the page pointed to https://app.shiftrwa.xyz, which redirected to /coming-soon; on 2026-09-17 the page points to shift-rwa.vercel.app/app, and both https://shift-rwa.vercel.app/app and https://app.shiftrwa.xyz/ return HTTP 200 client-rendered pages. Neither publishes a reserve figure: the Vercel app renders "TSL2L $0.00" and "TSL1S $0.00" under Top Movers, and app.shiftrwa.xyz returns an empty SPA shell. Rendered in a headed Chrome on 2026-09-24T02:03:20Z (document.body.innerText, agent-browser 0.31.1), app.shiftrwa.xyz is now a TSL2L trading page (a TSLL price chart, Buy/Sell, Connect Wallet) whose copy says "Custody of the Series assets held by Alpaca Markets; reserves are verified continuously." It still shows no reserve figure, no PoR feed and no attestation, so the assertion stays unevidenced. The earlier marketing site states PoR is "coming with mainnet". The on-chain record contradicts the gating claim outright: every observed issuance is a bare SPL Token-2022 mintTo signed by the mint's own authority keypair plus a fee payer, with no SHIFT program, oracle account or PoR account in the transaction at all. RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY 2026-09-18, and this is now a negative finding rather than an unlocated one: Chainlink's reference-data directory was read directly - reference-data-directory.vercel.app/feeds-mainnet.json (295 feeds) and /feeds-solana-mainnet.json (12 feeds) - and contains no SHIFT feed on either network; the only entry matching the string "shift" is Coinshift's "USPC NAV". The promise is dated: a 2025-05-21 report of SHIFT joining the Chainlink BUILD programme says "To increase user trust, SHIFT will integrate Chainlink's Proof of Reserve for its tokenized assets", i.e. sixteen months of "will". So the gating claim - "the SHIFT smart contract cannot issue tokens in excess of verified reserves; mint operations are gated by PoR feed" - has no feed to gate on, in addition to having no program in any observed mint transaction.

redemption.eligibility: Contradicted between primary documents. Each Series Operating Agreement grants a member a redemption right: "If a Member wishes to transfer their token back to the Series in exchange for funds, this is an internal membership-interest repurchase ... This transaction is available only to Members processed by smart contract where the transaction is settled directly from the treasury to the Member's wallet, not using any third-party assets." The Technical Overview says the opposite: "End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly. Mint and burn are B2B endpoints used by professional market makers to maintain inventory. Users acquire Series Tokens by swapping on Jupiter against market-maker liquidity." U.S. and U.K. persons are excluded from membership entirely.
redemption.rails: Documented retail path: internal membership-interest repurchase settled from the Series treasury by smart contract. Documented operational path: market makers mint and burn against the underlying ETF through B2B endpoints, 24/5 in line with U.S. trading hours, while user-facing trading is 24/7 RFQ on Jupiter, Meteora, Kamino and Orca. No burn address, latency, SLA or minimum is published for either path, and no SHIFT program exists on-chain to implement the smart-contract repurchase.
redemption.fees: Primary market: "The per-token purchase price shall equal the executed market price paid in a bona fide transaction to acquire one (1) share of [the named ETF], plus a transaction fee equal to 0.1% of such executed price." Ongoing: "The Master DAO is allowed to charge operational fees to the Series using a percentage-of-treasury formula" - the percentage is never stated in the master or any Series agreement. Secondary market: "User-facing trading costs are reflected in the RFQ spread quoted by market makers", tightest in U.S. hours and widest at weekends; the two docs pages give different weekend ceilings ("up to ~3%" in Solution Overview, "up to ~5%" in Risk Management). No transfer fee is charged on-chain: none of the eight mints carries a transferFeeConfig extension.

corporateActions: Nothing is passed through and nothing is applied by Shift. "Membership interests represent a limited economic interest in the Assets of the Series 17 treasury and do not provide any expectation of profit, income, or dividends." Leverage resets are the ETF issuer's: "SHIFT does not perform rebalancing. The leverage is delivered by the underlying ETF (e.g., Direxion TSLL), which manages its own daily reset internally. SHIFT simply tokenizes the ETF position 1:1. Nothing happens at 4 PM ET inside the SHIFT protocol." Wind-down is issuer-decided: on a "Master Cancellation Event" the Master DAO alone determines, in its administrative capacity, whether each Series "(i) continue[s] as an independent DAO LLC" or "(ii) be dissolved and wound up", and "all applicable fees, costs, and third-party expenses associated with such continuation shall be borne by the applicable Series or its members". Membership can also end involuntarily - "the person's involuntary immediate automatic withdrawal of their status as a Member, if the person is deemed a Restricted Person" - and Art. VII.2 provides that voluntary or involuntary cessation "does not give rise to any right of a Member to a distribution of any property or economic resources". Separately, the scaledUiAmountConfig authority on every mint lets the issuer restate all displayed balances; SOX3S already sits at multiplier 0.1.

pricing.notes: The issuer publishes no NAV, mark or indicative value for any Series Token at any cadence, and no oracle carries a price for them (rwa-sonar's own reference-price probe returns refSource null for all 8: "leveraged; no 1:1 reference"; the Shift symbols also truncate their underlyings, TSL2L to TSL and SOX3L to SOX, so no ticker join is possible). The user-facing price is a market maker's RFQ quote "based on the underlying ETF's NAV, plus a spread", and the spread is neither published nor bounded in any document. The primary-market price is anchored to a real exchange print - the executed price of one share of the named Direxion ETF plus 0.1% - so arbitrage against a public NAV is structurally possible, but only for the authorized market makers who can reach the mint/burn endpoints, and only 24/5. Observed secondary market on 2026-09-16: Jupiter reports null DEX liquidity on all eight mints, USD 117.91 of total 24h volume across all of them, organicScore 0 on every one, and a first pool for only 3 of 8 (all created 2026-07-31).

keyGovernance.evidence: Verified 2026-09-16 by RPC. Each mint has its own single authority address that simultaneously holds mintAuthority, freezeAuthority, permanentDelegate, metadataUpdateAuthority, pause and scaled-UI authority (SPX3L CoghvrToe8SZTta5Q6cb2BnVki6WXXGMogeSiea5vNte; SPX3S 2CeU1GEWbhXXZvypMfAPa2AzyvF3yhrG7AqUyFoDqxZf; TSL2L 21bymdv3CB8QFa5taouuTcrgTVLjH9vKVEScEKqKGRZd; TSL1S 9eo5QkvdxsAU6kdAbAABWpbq1TGvsxPkLoroPwgxY4o1; SOX3L 2g5JvVx2C6si9XoLoMjr1CEyK8Mt597qptsrNN1RZ4WB; SOX3S 76ThePy3xFjiAvEn2dxymehQJBGoD2vywfYVNgXGVJVA; SPCX2L ELt7GJcL4jxVoF1snNjxjegPKjuELxi13ut5f8R7vgH; SPCX2S 4mU3jH1iEA78LJ9YPfFYnN4ABty6xMBxndajFg3iToaK). getMultipleAccounts returns null for all eight, i.e. they are unfunded, dataless addresses, and each one nevertheless appears as a true transaction signer on raw Token-2022 mintTo instructions with a separate funded fee payer (2HfsYtL44s9FXVjit21VUfvW4fP6FvvqHHWNan6puTWz) - so they are plain off-chain Ed25519 keypairs, not program-derived addresses (a PDA cannot sign at the transaction level) and not Squads or any other multisig (no multisig program appears in any of the transactions). Recorded as hot-key with that nuance: single-key control, fees sponsored by another wallet. The mints themselves were created on 2026-05-12 to 2026-06-11 by HJfhNwwaDqcUc7k5J8N5y3y1xHZ7qDYMsC7YFpp9fCdp with a plain createAccount + initialize* + setAuthority script. No threshold, timelock or governance process is disclosed for any of these keys, and none of the eight addresses appears in any Shift document. The rebase (scaledUiAmountConfig) authority is the same per-mint key that already holds mint, freeze, pause, metadata and permanent delegate — eight distinct keys, one per mint — so it inherits their 'hot-key' characterisation. The mechanism is in use, not merely armed: SOX3S (authority 76ThePy3xFjiAvEn2dxymehQJBGoD2vywfYVNgXGVJVA) reads a multiplier of 0.1, so a displayed SOX3S balance is already one tenth of its raw amount.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: Membership is defined by token holding: "A person becomes a Member by obtaining at least one (1) [Series] SHFT Token", and each holder "shall be deemed to have agreed to and be bound by this Agreement upon such person's acquiring" it. The Series records required by Art. VI.1 are "the name of each current and former Member or the unique Distributed Ledger identifier(s) attributable to each Member", and where the activity is on a distributed ledger with public human-readable explanations "there shall be no separate requirement to keep books of accounts". No transfer agent, share register or off-chain holder list exists anywhere in the documents. The caveat that keeps this from being clean: the agreements never name the mint, locating the token smart contract at "an address and a blockchain to be determined", so the chain is the register of a Series whose own agreement does not identify which chain or which mint.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Nothing gates a transfer today, on any of the eight mints: defaultAccountState is initialized (new accounts are not frozen), the transferHook slot is initialized with a null programId, there is no allowlist, and there is no transferFeeConfig at all. Any wallet can send to any wallet, and the tokens are marketed as "24/7 permissionless" and composable on Jupiter, Meteora, Kamino and Orca. Control is entirely reactive: the permanentDelegate, freeze and pause powers are exercised after the fact, and the Risk Disclosure says a U.S. or U.K. person who bypasses the restrictions "may result in immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation of the associated tokens without recourse".

bearerRedemption.reason: Presenting the token compels delivery from nobody. The Series Operating Agreement's repurchase right is to be "processed by smart contract", and no SHIFT program exists on-chain to process it - every observed issuance is a raw Token-2022 mintTo by a keypair. The Technical Overview states plainly that "End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly" and that mint and burn are "B2B endpoints used by professional market makers", the app that would front a redemption resolves to /coming-soon, backing operations run only 24/5, and U.S. and U.K. persons are barred from membership entirely. Observed burns are negligible: on SOX3L the sum of all mintTo amounts (3,967.41007219) exceeds current supply (3,967.37399156) by 0.03608063 tokens, i.e. about 0.0009% of supply has ever been retired.

forcedTransfers.reason: Confirmed in both law and code. All eight mints carry a live permanentDelegate plus freezeAuthority and pausableConfig, all three held by the same single key per mint. The Risk Disclosure authorises the use: any attempt by a U.S. or U.K. person to bypass the restrictions "including the use of VPNs or proxy entities - is a material breach of the Operational Agreement and may result in immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation of the associated tokens without recourse", and Art. VII of each Series agreement makes Restricted-Person status trigger "involuntary immediate automatic withdrawal" of membership with no right to a distribution.

titleDeed.reason: The site-wide legal notice is explicit: holding the tokens "does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets", and each Series "is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by" the trademark owners it references. Even on the Series agreements' more generous reading ("treasury ownership only"), the treasury asset is a Direxion daily-reset leveraged ETF share, not the referenced equity, so the token is at best a derived interest two layers away from Tesla or the S&P 500.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Ordinary Token-2022 mints, held in any Solana wallet: "Holders custody the token in any Solana wallet. There is no liquidation engine and no forced close", and "SPL tokens held in any Solana wallet. No exchange custody." No KYC or allowlist gates holding, and Phantom, OKX Wallet and other wallets are listed integrations.

issuerIndependent.reason: The token cannot outlive its administrator on its own terms. On a "Master Cancellation Event" the Master DAO alone decides whether each Series continues as an independent DAO LLC or is wound up, and the members pay for continuation. The documented value chain runs entirely through parties the holder cannot reach: an unnamed "private entity that holds the backing assets", unnamed market makers who alone can mint and burn, and an administrator that owes no fiduciary duty and is subject to no court action in any jurisdiction. Nothing independent of Shift attests the reserve, and no NAV or PoR feed exists to price the token if Shift stopped publishing.

presetJurisdiction.reason: Unusually well pinned down for this cohort. A named issuer (SHIFT DAO LLC), a named jurisdiction (Republic of the Marshall Islands, DAO Act 2022 and LLC Act 1996), a stated governing law (RMI, in both the Terms of Use and every Series agreement), a named nominee member with a Majuro address (MINS LLC, Trust Company Complex, Ajeltake Road) and a fixed forum (ICDR arbitration seated in the RMI). The flag asks whether the jurisdiction is preset, and it is; what the jurisdiction is worth is another matter, since the agreements bar any court action anywhere and remove both fiduciary duties and inspection rights.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Every third-party verification Shift claims is either absent or somebody else's. Chainlink Proof-of-Reserves is described as running "continuously" and publishing "every block" and as gating mints, yet the PoR dashboard link reads "[TO BE UPDATED]", no Chainlink PoR feed naming SHIFT could be located, and the observed mints carry no oracle account at all. The "Third-party attestation" heading in the Collateral & Custody page is an empty "[TO BE UPDATED]". The sole file on the Audits page is a Zokyo review of ARTokens GmbH's Ethereum ERC-20 contract dated 19 June 2025. No custodian confirmation, holdings statement or reconciliation output has ever been published by DekaBank, ALPACADB LTD or anyone else.

aiReady.reason: Follows the definition: unconditionalTransfers is yes and tokenSelfCustody is yes, so an agent can hold and trade these tokens with no KYC and no allowlist. Three caveats that the flag does not capture: an agent cannot truthfully make the non-U.S./non-U.K.-person representation membership requires, it holds an asset subject to clawback, freeze and global pause by a single key, and there is effectively no market to trade into - USD 117.91 of 24h volume across all eight mints and no reported DEX liquidity on any of them.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: The mechanism exists but no document binds it to a legal process. The clawback, freeze and pause powers are triggered by the issuer's own determination - Restricted-Person status or "a material breach of the Operational Agreement" such as VPN use - not by a court or regulator, and no procedure, notice period or appeal is published. The Restricted-Person definition does track external legal instruments (the UN Security Council Consolidated List and OFAC-embargoed regions), which is the one point in Shift's favour, but the same agreements bar any court action "in any court of any jurisdiction" and remove inspection rights, so there is no ordinary forum in which a holder-facing order could be obtained and then reflected on-chain.

meetingOfMinds.reason: A DEX or peer-to-peer transfer settles on the agreement of buyer and seller alone: no issuer signature, allowlist check, transfer hook or KYC step sits in the transfer path on any of the eight mints. Validity can be undone afterwards by clawback or freeze, but the transfer itself needs no third party.

openQuestions: Which document controls? The executed Series agreements say "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and grant "treasury ownership only", while the site-wide legal notice says holding the tokens gives no "legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets". The whole claim-depth grade turns on this and the issuer publishes both.

Which mint does each Series Operating Agreement actually govern? Every agreement locates the token in "the Smart Contract located at an address and a blockchain to be determined", and the Series 17 (S&P 500) agreement requires "at least one (1) TSLA Short SHFT Token". Nothing published links the mints that trade to the Series that hold the assets.

What backs SPCX2L and SPCX2S, and under what Series? Both mints are live and trading, neither appears in the docs' Series or contract-address tables, and no Operating Agreement exists. Direxion's 2x SpaceX bull ETF (LOFF) listed on NYSE Arca on 15 June per Structured Retail Products, and a bear counterpart (LOFD) was announced later - was either instrument held when 250 SPCX2L were minted on 2026-06-16 and 395.72 SPCX2S on 2026-06-24?

ANSWERED (2026-09-18): no. The Chainlink Proof-of-Reserves integration that the docs describe as gating every mint and publishing every block does not exist. Chainlink's own reference-data directory was read end to end on both networks - 295 Ethereum-mainnet feeds and 12 Solana-mainnet feeds - and contains no SHIFT feed; the only entry matching "shift" is Coinshift's USPC NAV. The dashboard link is still "[TO BE UPDATED]", no observed mint transaction touches an oracle or reserve account, and the integration has been announced as forthcoming since 2025-05-21, when SHIFT joined the Chainlink BUILD programme ("SHIFT will integrate Chainlink's Proof of Reserve for its tokenized assets"). Recorded in findings as no-reserve-verification-published, severity critical. What remains open is only whether it is still intended: Chainlink Labs has said it is concluding BUILD-programme arrangements.

Is there any SHIFT Solana program? The docs describe "the SHIFT Solana program" that "mints, burns, and tracks Series Token supply" and audited "open-source" contracts, but every observed issuance is a raw Token-2022 mintTo signed by a bare keypair.

PARTLY ANSWERED (2026-09-18), and the answer is circumstantial rather than documentary. ARTokens GmbH is "an Austrian token issuer" registered at Simmeringer Hauptstrasse 24, Vienna, issuing asset-referenced tokens under MiCAR, whose own site advertises exactly Shift's pitch: "Backing asset reserves are verified via Chainlink Proof of Reserve and periodic audits". Four of the employer names on Shift's anonymous team page turn up as roles on ARTokens' named one - a "Flow Traders former CTO" as CTO, a "Securitize former Software Engineer and Architect" who is also "ex- CheckPoint", and an "ex-Utila" VP R&D. And the 2025-05-21 Chainlink BUILD report describes SHIFT itself as "building Asset-Referenced Tokens (ARTokens) - MiCAR-compliant digital assets backed by stocks, bonds, and ETFs". Suggestive of a shared team or a shared lineage; NOT proof of affiliation, and no corporate link is disclosed on either side. It still does not make a Zokyo review of ARTokens' Ethereum ERC-20 "aRtoken.sol" an audit of these eight Solana mints, which is what Shift's Audits page uses it for.
Why is SOX3S on a scaled-UI multiplier of 0.1 when the other seven mints are on 1? No document mentions the multiplier.
What is the Master DAO's percentage-of-treasury fee? Both the master and the Series agreements authorise it and neither states a number.

Which restriction list binds? There are now FOUR, from one issuer, and they do not agree. (1) The executed Series agreements - the only documents a Series member is actually party to - define Restricted Persons as UN-listed persons plus residents of Iran, Syria, Cuba, North Korea and Crimea/Donetsk/Luhansk, and do NOT exclude U.S. or U.K. persons. (2) The Terms of Use, Risk Disclosure and site notice exclude U.S. and U.K. persons explicitly and threaten "immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation". (3) The vaults-only Terms add OFAC and any "list of prohibited or restricted parties", exclude the United States by name, and name 24 jurisdictions. (4) The vaults KYC/AML page repeats those 24 and then extends to the whole FATF blacklist and greylist - "jurisdictions identified by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) as High-Risk Jurisdictions subject to a Call for Action or Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring" - and says screening is enforced pre-block by the sequencer. Lists (3) and (4) are written for the vaults product, so a Series holder cannot tell whether they apply; the binding agreement remains the narrowest of the four. ANSWERED (2026-09-23): as a matter of contract, list (1) binds and it alone decides membership; the others bind only the use of a website or of a different product. (a) A Series member's contract is the Series Operating Agreement, which a person accepts by acquiring the token (Art. III) and which says "This Agreement represents the entire agreement among all the Members and between the Members and the Series and the Company" (Art. XII.1). It defines "Restricted Person" itself (Art. VIII.2: UN-listed persons and residents of Iran, Syria, Cuba, North Korea, Crimea, Donetsk and Luhansk), so the Master Agreement's wider list, which does name the United States, is not imported: the Series agreement borrows Master definitions only for capitalised terms "used but not otherwise defined", and the Master list governs membership of the Master DAO, which a Series member may but need not hold. The only consequence the Series agreement attaches to the list is automatic cessation of membership without a distribution (Art. VII(ii), VII.2). Its only hierarchy clause (Art. XII.5) ranks the Certificate of Formation and the Agreement above the smart contract; nothing ranks any website document above it or incorporates one into it. (b) The Terms of Use say "These Terms govern your use of the Website" and defer on the interests themselves to "the relevant operating agreement published on the website"; they contain no entire-agreement or precedence clause. Their U.S.-inclusive list (s. 9) controls access to the governance interface, not membership. (c) The Risk Disclosure calls a U.S. or U.K. person's acquisition "a material breach of the Operational Agreement" with "immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation", but the Series agreement contains no such exclusion and no such remedy. That sentence describes a term the agreement does not have and adds nothing to it. The technical power to do it exists: a single hot key per mint holds freeze and permanent-delegate authority. (d) The vaults Terms cover the Interface and "any other products or services that link to this Agreement". No Series agreement links to them, so they bind a Series holder only in that person's use of the vaults. The result: a U.S. or U.K. person who buys a Series token on Jupiter becomes a member under the only contract in point, is in breach of the website terms if they used the website, and is exposed to an issuer freeze or forced transfer that no document gives a contractual basis for. That gap is the risk, and securities and sanctions law apply to them regardless. Unsettled: no RMI court has construed these documents; RMI LLC law follows Delaware, where an operating agreement with an integration clause is read as written.

Where did "over $40M in liquidity" go? Press reporting from the June 2026 Jupiter listing cites that figure; on 2026-09-16 Jupiter reports no DEX liquidity on any Shift mint, USD 3.26M of combined market cap and USD 117.91 of 24h volume.

Is the leveraged programme still being invested in, or is it being succeeded? www.shiftrwa.xyz now leads with covered-call vaults on SPY and COPX while /faq, /markets, /blog, /status and the Operating Agreement PDFs 404 on that domain and survive only on a Vercel preview host.
Who is the market maker with mint and burn access, and who is the "private entity that holds the backing assets"? Neither is named, and both sit between the holder and the ETF.

Does the RMI "international investment business license and registration number 10246-26" claimed on the vaults Legal & Compliance page exist, and would it cover the Series tokens? The number appears nowhere else - not in any Series Operating Agreement, the Master agreement, the Terms of Use, the Risk Disclosure or the site-wide legal notice, all of which deny authorised status - and no public searchable Marshall Islands register of such licences was located, so it is recorded as unverified. It also sits oddly beside the same issuer's position that the interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law".

Do the vaults-only legal pages bind a Series holder at all? Four documents that a holder would reasonably read as Shift's legal terms - Legal & Compliance, KYC/AML, Bankruptcy Remote Structure and the vaults FAQ - are written for Shift Vaults (stablecoin staking and secured lending to OpenTrade SPC, a Cayman SPC with an independent board and an FCA-regulated operator). They carry a different arbitration forum, a class-action waiver, wider restriction lists, an OFAC screening regime, freeze-and-seize smart-contract powers and a bankruptcy-remote structure that the Series tokens do not have. Nothing on the legal hub tells a Series holder which pages govern them. ANSWERED (2026-09-23): no, not as a Series holder. The vaults Terms define their own scope as the Interface and "any other products or services that link to this Agreement"; no Series Operating Agreement links to them, and each Series agreement declares itself the entire agreement between member, Series and Company (Art. XII.1). They bind a person as a vaults user. For a Series holder they are evidence of what the issuer intends, not terms of the holding.

DAO Act 2022 s.703(2)(a) switches off the RMI Securities and Investment Act only "To the extent that a DAO LLC is not, directly or indirectly, issuing … any digital securities … to residents of the Republic", and s.703(2)(d) exempts only a governance token "conferring no economic rights" - which a Series token, by its own definition, is not. So the RMI position is a jurisdictional carve-out rather than a finding that these are not securities, and outside the RMI the issuer simply disclaims registration everywhere. The SEC’s January 2026 statement points the other way for the product class: "The format in which a security is issued or the methods by which holders are recorded (e.g. onchain vs. offchain) does not affect application of the federal securities laws", and it describes a "linked security" - a third party’s instrument giving synthetic exposure to a referenced security - as itself a security. Also live: the Risk Disclosure’s trademark paragraph, under which a Series "may need to change marketing materials, token naming conventions, or public disclosures", and DAO Act s.714(1)(d) dissolution by the Registrar where a DAO LLC no longer performs a lawful purpose.

whatIf.outcome: You cannot go to court at all: after 30 days’ notice the Series agreement sends every dispute to a sole ICDR arbitrator seated in the Marshall Islands, final and without appeal, and adds that "No action at law or in equity based upon any claim arising out of or related to this Agreement shall be instituted in any court of any jurisdiction." Worse, losing costs you the position: a determination that you are in material breach or acted against the Series’ best interests is itself a dissociation event, and dissociation pays nothing.

whatIf.note: THREE INCONSISTENT REGIMES from one issuer. (a) The executed Series agreements: "the Dispute shall be settled by arbitration administered by the International Centre for Dispute Resolution in accordance with its International Arbitration Rules (the "Rules"). The arbitration shall be seated in the Republic of the Marshall Islands and governed by the laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands. The language of the arbitration shall be English." plus the court bar quoted above - a sole arbitrator, RMI seat, RMI law, no appeal, and a defendant (the Series) whose assets you cannot inspect (Art. VI.2) and which owes you no fiduciary duty (Art. IV.3). (b) The Terms of Use, section 12: "you agree to submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of RMI" - the opposite of the agreement’s bar. (c) The vaults-only Terms: ICC rather than ICDR arbitration, plus an express "You agree that any disputes will be resolved on an individual basis, and you waive any right to participate in a class action lawsuit or class-wide arbitration." No class or consolidation provision appears in the Series agreements at all, so collective redress is not waived there so much as unaddressed - and bilateral arbitration with a sole arbitrator achieves the same result. The sting is Art. XII.2.C: "C. In the event that it is determined pursuant to this Article XII that a Member who is party to a Dispute (i) is in material breach of this Agreement, (ii) acts in material violation of any statutory requirements of the Republic of the Marshall Islands or the laws or regulations of any other applicable jurisdiction, or (iii) acts against the best interests of the Series, such determination shall be deemed a Dissociation Event, as defined in Article VIII, for such Member." - i.e. an adverse arbitral finding triggers Art. VII dissociation, and Art. VII.2 gives a dissociated member no right to any distribution. RMI law preserves narrow court routes the agreement purports to close: LLC Act s.79(11) ("the High Court, upon cause shown, may wind up the affairs of the series upon application of any member associated with the series, the member’s personal representative or assignee, and in connection therewith, may appoint a liquidating trustee."), s.79(12), s.47 and the derivative action under s.61, all in the High Court of the Republic; whether the contractual bar survives against them is untested. No arbitration or court proceeding involving Shift, SHIFT DAO LLC or any Series was found on CourtListener or the general web.
